name: CI runner-pod hook failures — a burst of self-hosted jobs failed within 60 s of starting (presumed ARC hook failure by shape)
description: Fires when, in the trailing 10 min, at least 3 jobs of ONE workflow run (breakdown ci.run_id) on the self-hosted pool (ci.runner.kind=self-hosted) concluded failure with duration_ms under 60000. This is a HEURISTIC, presumed by shape, not a read of the failing step: the github-ci dataset carries each job's conclusion, runner kind and duration but NO step name or error text, and a job that fails within a minute of starting failed before any real step could run — the ARC Kubernetes hook could not bring the workflow pod up ('Executing the custom container implementation failed', typically 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.43.0.1:443' while k3s was restarting). Calibrated on the 2026-09-06 06:07Z incident: run 34015621705 attempt 1 had 16 such jobs at 26-46 s (conclusion=failure, self-hosted) against the re-run's 16 successes at 24-295 s — query https://ui.honeycomb.io/thewoolleyweb/environments/livespec/datasets/github-ci/result/zG6ThT4a81m. One flaky fast job must not page; a burst does, hence >= 3 per run. This is the DURABLE detection of hook failures: the node-side sweep's hook-failure class (ci-runner/k3s/phase2/runner-pod-lifecycle/scan-runner-pod-lifecycle.sh) greps LIVE runner-pod logs and misses every failure whose ephemeral runner pod is already gone, which is most of them; the sweep's api-unavailable class names the k3s restart that usually causes the burst. Runbook: ssh poweredge-xubuntu; sudo journalctl -u scan-runner-pod-lifecycle -n 80 --no-pager (api-unavailable, containerd-deadline); sudo journalctl -u k3s -p err --since -1h; re-run the failed jobs on the SAME commit once the host is back — it is not a test failure. Data: .github/scripts/export-ci-telemetry.sh (export-telemetry). livespec-kgdlte, plan ci-runner-pod-lifecycle-reliability.
